basis: Penile carcinoma has a reproductive site outside the axes; HPV causation alone does not classify the malignancy as an infection.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: this concept is a carcinoma caused by HPV, rather than an infection, immunodeficiency, immune-mediated disease or lymphoma.

basis: Glyoxylate metabolic disorder with defining renal oxalate injury; stones occur in 80-99%. Hepatic enzyme deficiency does not establish liver damage; anemia need not reflect direct blood injury.

decisions.renal: primary: nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis and progressive renal injury define the clinical disease; stones occur in 80-99%.

basis: Paraplegia, intellectual disability, nephropathy and deafness define the syndrome (80-99%). Hypertension (30-79%) is a secondary renal complication, without established direct vascular disease.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: hypertension is annotated in 30-79%, but is a separately diagnosed consequence of nephropathy rather than direct cardiovascular involvement.

basis: Scrotal malignancies predominantly affect scrotal skin, most commonly as squamous carcinoma; this supports dermatologic origin across the umbrella.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the scrotum is a cutaneous sac, and most scrotal cancers arise in its skin despite classification under reproductive-system cancers.

basis: Phenylalanine metabolic disorder explicitly defined by cognitive impairment, seizures and developmental dysfunction; neurological manifestations are defining features.

decisions.neurologic: primary: the supplied definition explicitly characterizes this phenotype by cognitive impairment, seizures and developmental disorders.

basis: Intellectual disability and alpha-thalassemia define ATR-X; talipes and visual impairment each occur in 30-79%. Reflux (80-99%) alone does not establish direct GI damage.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: reflux is annotated in 80-99%, but direct GI injury or intrinsic dysmotility is not established by the supplied phenotype.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: talipes equinovarus is a structural skeletal defect occurring in 30-79%; spinal deformities provide additional support.

basis: Immunodeficiency and autoimmunity are explicit defining mechanisms; skeletal and metabolic abnormalities vary between SHORT and immunodeficiency subtypes.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: skeletal abnormalities characterize SHORT presentations, but substantial skeletal damage in most patients across this umbrella is not established.

basis: Cardiac, skeletal and CNS malformations are core patterns; renal defects occur in 80-99%. Ocular, otologic and oral malformations, also annotated 80-99%, omitted at cap.

decisions.neurologic: primary: CNS malformations are a major embryopathy pattern; microcephaly is annotated 80-99%, with hydrocephalus and brain/spinal malformations in 30-79%.

basis: Bile-duct paucity, intellectual disability and meatal atresia define syndrome; clubfeet are major diagnostic defects. VSD and low immunoglobulins (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: VSD occurs in 30-79% and qualifies, but is omitted at the four-axis cap in favor of defining hepatic, neurologic, otologic and skeletal defects.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: clubfeet are explicitly defining structural defects, meeting the major-diagnostic-feature exception without a numerical frequency.
decisions.otologic: primary: external auditory meatal atresia is part of the defining branchial dysplasia, establishing structural ear involvement.

basis: Cutaneous hamartoma defined by proliferation of eccrine sweat glands and capillary vessels; its vascular component is intrinsic to the lesion.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: proliferating capillary vessels are a defining component, supported by the benign vascular tumor parent; this is intrinsic vascular pathology.
